text:
Sam: FYI — big customer escalation from FinData Inc. says behavior changed after last week's model rollout. internal evals are green but their prompt now returns hallucinated account numbers. attaching excerpt from CS convo.

Nora: Copy of customer message: 'Our fraud flags used to return a single consolidated identifier. After the update we get multiple inconsistent IDs and one is obviously fabricated.' they've attached a failing request id: req_0a3f2c.

Sam: Repro steps I tried (same payload) vs their result: our hosted endpoint returns the expected short id. customer claims same model name but different output.

Maria: Which model variant did they pin to? canary rollout history shows redwood-v1.3-ffnpatch -> promoted 2026-01-22 02:10 UTC. customer said they didn't pin.

Sam: Customer screenshot shows model header: redwood-v1.3 (no quant suffix). They might have been routed to the canary variant.

Luca: Quick checklist: tokenizer, system prompt, temperature/top_p, sampling seed. Also check if their payload includes 'stop' tokens or post-processing in their app. internal eval suite uses deterministic sampling (temp=0). customers often call with temp=0.2.

Nora: I asked customer for the raw curl they used. they sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1.3","input":"Generate consolidated account identifier for: ACCOUNT_SUMMARY...","temperature":0.2}'
```

Maria: aha — our internal eval ran with temperature=0.0 (greedy). margin for hallucination rises at 0.2. But that doesn't fully explain a change after rollout if previous variant behaved. we need a diff in decoding behavior or system prompt changes.

Luca: Also compare tokenizer behavior: the new ffn patch had a subtle tokenization reorder that can change generation for numerics. I'll run a tokenization diff on their prompt.

Sam: Customer says they used the same payload last week and only started seeing issues after 2026-01-22.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout event: redwood-v1.3-ffnpatch promoted from canary to 30% traffic at 2026-01-22T02:10:14Z (trace rollout_id=rl_78f2).

Maria: I'm running a controlled repro now against both redwood-v1.2 and redwood-v1.3-ffnpatch with temp=0.2 and top_p=0.9. attaching quick outputs.

Maria: redwood-v1.2 -> "ACC-87122" (expected)

Maria: redwood-v1.3-ffnpatch -> "ACC-87122, ACC-00000" (extra fabricated id)

Luca: That shows variant-specific behavior. Next: run tokenization and log kv-cache attention patterns for the final generation. also compare position embeddings handling for long tokens.

Aj: From a product POV, can we confirm if this affects only numeric-ish prompts or broader customers? we should triage impact scope before deciding rollback.

Nora: Customer reported 2 other accounts with same pattern. I'll ask for consent to run their exact requests in our staging with logging and to share any PII-removed payloads.

Maria: Preliminary hypothesis: FFN patch changed exact logits around numeric separator tokens, increasing probability mass for another id token sequence when temperature>0. Our internal evals didn't include that customer prompt family (they're edge-case numeric consolidation).

Luca: Proposed immediate steps: 1) add customer's prompt to eval harness (priority) 2) repro on dedicated canary fleet with logs (we need kv cache & logits) 3) if confirmed regression, either rollback redwood-v1.3-ffnpatch or deploy microfix (temp normalization / post-filter) 4) notify CS and customer timeline.

Sam: Customer is asking for ETA and whether we can roll back. they are on a billable production integration.

Maria: Running logits capture now. also checking if quantization path or compiler kernel selection triggered for their routing (some hosts use int8 path).

Luca: One gotcha: our eval suite normalizes IDs before comparing (strip punctuation), so the metric passed even if model appended extra tokens. that explains internal green. we need strict string equality tests for these prompts.

Nora: Noted — will inform customer we're investigating and may request sample requests. trying to buy time: "we're prioritizing this, could you please send a redacted request body and the full response headers (including X-Request-ID)".

Aj: If this is variant-only and affects many customers, rollback is the right call. if it's narrow, a targeted fix + improved evaluation coverage is better. we should prepare both paths.

Maria: Update: reproduced on dedicated canary host with trace id req_0a3f2c replicated. captured logits show a secondary peak at the fabricated id tokens starting at step 34. attaching masked log excerpt: 
```
step 33: token="," logit=-0.12 prob=0.10
step 34: token=" ACC" logit=0.85 prob=0.34  <-- unexpected boost
step 35: token="-00000" logit=0.79 prob=0.29
```

Luca: That logit boost aligns with the FFN kernel reorder affecting certain hash buckets in the token projection. low-prob but nonzero at temp=0.2 leads to extra token.

Sam: Customer is pushing for a rollback. can we get a quick risk assessment?

Maria: Risk of rollback: loses the ffm perf/regressions improvements; risk of keeping: customer outages + more reports. I'd recommend rolling redwood-v1.3 back to previous baseline for all traffic and keep ffnpatch in 0% until we patch.

Aj: Approve rollback if impact is multi-customer. Maria/Luca, please confirm number of customers impacted within 2 hours. Nora, prep customer comms template.

Nora: Will do. Draft: "we've identified a model variant regression affecting some numeric consolidation prompts. we are prioritizing a rollback and will update within 2 hours." :thumbsup:

Maria: I'll start rollback plan. deploying rollback on canary now, then scale to 100% if clean. notifying infra.

deploy-bot: Rollback scheduled: rollback_id=rb_33a1, initiated 2026-01-22T04:03:04Z, target model redwood-v1.3 -> redwood-v1.2 baseline.

Sam: Thanks team. post-rollback we'll add the customer's prompt to the regression suite and update docs about tokenizer edge cases. I'll keep the customer updated.

Luca: Action items noted: add strict string-equality tests for sensitive ID prompts; add token-level log collection toggle for triage; review FFN patch kernel for hash bucket instability.

Maria: Final note: internal evals need to include temp=range tests (0, 0.2, 0.5) for critical prompt families. caught this gap.

Sam: Closing loop: customer acknowledged the rollback plan and asked for a follow-up call after stability checks.
